stemMd: A committee rejected a proposal last year. Its chair now argues that the proposal must be unsound because the committee rejected it. The argument is most vulnerable because it

options.label: A
options.textMd: confuses future costs with past costs.

options.label: B
options.textMd: assumes the proposal was never considered.

options.label: C
options.textMd: shows that every committee decision is unreliable.

options.label: D
options.textMd: relies on a statistically unrepresentative survey.

options.label: E
options.textMd: treats the earlier decision as sufficient evidence for the merits of that same decision.

explanationMd: A decision may have been made for weak reasons, procedural reasons, or reasons no longer applicable. Merely repeating that rejection occurred supplies no independent assessment of whether the proposal is unsound.

distractorRationale.b: It expressly says it was rejected.
distractorRationale.c: It gives no evidence of universal unreliability.
